steps.description: On the reconciled 120-sample count matrix, pre-filter low-count genes with edgeR::filterByExpr (min 10 counts in at least the smaller group's sample count), TMM-normalize with edgeR, then fit limma-voom with a fixed-effects design (~condition), explicit reference level = control, contrast = case vs control. Report the moderated-t statistic, unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken (or equivalent limma eBayes) log2 fold changes, BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering, at alpha 0.05. steps.name: Case vs control classifier with nested cross-validation
steps.context: n=120 (60/60), unpaired, single batch, whole blood. No external validation cohort is available in the provided files. The research question explicitly asks 'how accurate would it be on a new sample,' which nested CV addresses only as an internal estimate.
steps.question: Can a gene-expression-based classifier distinguish case from control whole-blood samples, and what is an honest internal estimate of its accuracy (ROC-AUC, sensitivity/specificity) on a held-out sample from this cohort?

grounding.reason: Classifier of sample class from expression: penalized logistic regression with nested CV, ROC-AUC + CI, feature filtering inside folds, per R-0155@b81f.

steps.description: Build a binary classifier of case vs control from the reconciled, filtered, TMM-normalized log-CPM gene expression matrix (the full filtered gene set from T1S1's filterByExpr output, not restricted to the significant DE genes — using the DE-derived list would be a feature selection performed outside cross-validation and would inflate performance). Fit a penalized logistic regression (glmnet, elastic net, alpha and lambda tuned) with a nested cross-validation: outer loop (e.g., 10-fold, repeated) estimates generalization performance; inner loop selects lambda/alpha and performs any further feature filtering/scaling strictly within the training fold only. Report the outer-fold ROC-AUC with a bootstrap or DeLong confidence interval (pROC), a calibration plot, sensitivity/specificity at a clinically reasonable operating point, and the genes with consistently nonzero coefficients across folds (noting instability given the sample size). Run a permutation-label negative control (shuffle case/control labels, repeat the nested CV) to confirm the true AUC exceeds the null distribution. State explicitly that this cross-validated estimate is the best available proxy for accuracy on a new sample from the same population and setting, but is not equivalent to performance on an independent external cohort, which does not exist in this dataset.

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control classifier + DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 121-sample (60 case/60 control) whole-blood bulk RNA-seq, gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 121 samples, one gene-symbol column plus 120 sample columns matching the 120-row metadata — note the counts file column count exceeds metadata rows by one, which the QC step must reconcile before any modeling). The research question has two parts: (1) can a classifier separate case from control, and (2) how accurate would it be on a new sample. Because each group holds >=50 samples, the knowledge-grounded procedure for this sample size flags that DESeq2/edgeR's negative-binomial models exaggerate false positives in population cohorts and prescribes limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model instead, with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a robustness control. The pipeline is: (T1S0) reconcile/QC the raw count matrix against metadata and inspect sample structure (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to catch sample-count mismatches, outliers, or unexpected clustering before any test; (T1S1) filter low-count genes with filterByExpr, TMM-normalize, and fit limma-voom for case vs control DE with apeglm-style effect reporting, BH-adjusted at alpha 0.05, with independent filtering and a Wilcoxon control; (T2S1) pathway enrichment (camera on the limma fit, Hallmark first, then Reactome/WikiPathways as follow-up collections, respecting the size window and the >=50 significant-gene rule for any ORA); (T3S1) the actual classifier — a penalized logistic regression (glmnet) built on the full filtered/normalized gene expression matrix (NOT restricted to the DE gene list, to avoid selection-bias leakage), with feature filtering and scaling performed inside each fold of a nested cross-validation, and performance reported as ROC-AUC with a confidence interval from the outer-loop held-out predictions plus calibration and a permutation-label negative control; (T4S1) an integrated report stating the classifier's expected real-world accuracy honestly, including the caveat that no external validation cohort exists so the CV estimate is the best available accuracy proxy, not a guarantee of generalization to a new clinical population.
